config.title: Capacitor GPS + Nearby Restaurants

intro.title: Capacitor GPS + Nearby Restaurants
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a mobile app that uses the device's GPS to find your current location and then displays a list of nearby restaurants. You will learn how to use Capacitor, a tool that lets you access native device features like GPS from your Angular web app. The core programming concept is integrating a native device API and handling asynchronous data, such as waiting for the GPS coordinates and fetching restaurant data. You'll work with Angular services, the Capacitor Geolocation plugin, and a mock API service to create a functional location-based feature.
intro.usecase: This pattern is essential for location-based mobile apps like food delivery services (Uber Eats, DoorDash), travel guides (TripAdvisor), and social check-in apps (Foursquare). Developers implement this to show users nearby restaurants, ATMs, or gas stations based on their real-time GPS coordinates. In practice, you'll build interfaces with maps, distance filters, and dynamic lists that update as users move. Mastering this combination of device sensors and API integration is crucial for creating engaging mobile experiences that respond to physical context.

objectives: Apply Angular CLI commands to generate new components and services for the application.
Implement Capacitor Geolocation API methods to access the device's current GPS coordinates.
Use Angular's HttpClient to make HTTP requests to a restaurant API endpoint.
Construct TypeScript interfaces to define the structure of restaurant data objects.
Execute conditional logic to handle GPS permission states and location errors.
Store retrieved GPS coordinates in component state variables for later use.
Utilize RxJS operators to transform API response data into usable restaurant listings.
Implement Angular template syntax to display restaurant information in the view.
Apply CSS styling to format restaurant cards with images, names, and distances.
Control user interface feedback by displaying loading indicators during API calls.
Define and invoke a function to calculate distances between user location and restaurant coordinates.
Modify component templates to conditionally show error messages when location services fail.

steps.title: Import Angular core and Capacitor Geolocation
steps.instruction: Import Component from '@angular/core' and Geolocation from '@capacitor/geolocation' in your TypeScript file.
steps.hint: Use the import statement with the correct package names. You'll need both imports for the upcoming steps.
steps.expectedOutcome: The file now has the necessary imports for creating an Angular component and using the Capacitor Geolocation plugin.
successCriteria: The code includes two import statements: one for Component from '@angular/core' and one for Geolocation from '@capacitor/geolocation'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the Angular Component decorator and the Capacitor Geolocation plugin. These are essential for building your GPS-enabled component.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check your import statements. Make sure you're importing Component from '@angular/core' and Geolocation from '@capacitor/geolocation' exactly as shown.
steps.feedbackWrong: Let's try again. You need to add two import statements: one for Component from '@angular/core' and another for Geolocation from '@capacitor/geolocation'.

steps.title: Create the main component class
steps.instruction: Create a class named LocationComponent and add the @Component decorator with an empty selector and template.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator from Angular core and define a class with the name LocationComponent.
steps.expectedOutcome: A LocationComponent class is created with the @Component decorator, ready for implementation.
successCriteria: The code should have a class named LocationComponent decorated with @Component, with empty selector and template strings.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the LocationComponent class with the @Component decorator. This sets up the basic Angular component structure.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've included both the @Component decorator with empty selector/template and the class named LocationComponent.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class isn't properly defined. Check that you've created a class named LocationComponent with the @Component decorator containing empty selector and template properties.

steps.instruction:
Add the @Component decorator with selector: 'app-location' and template: '

steps.hint: Place the @Component decorator just above the class definition. The selector should be 'app-location' and the template should be a simple empty div.

steps.title: Initialize location state properties
steps.instruction: Inside the LocationComponent class, add two public properties: 'latitude' of type number and 'longitude' of type number. Initialize them with default values (e.g., 0).
steps.hint: Add these properties directly in the class body, using TypeScript type annotations. For example: latitude: number = 0;
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class now has latitude and longitude properties that will store the user's GPS coordinates.
successCriteria: The component class contains two public properties: latitude (type number) and longitude (type number), both initialized with numeric default values.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the latitude and longitude properties to store location data. These will be used to hold the GPS coordinates we'll get from the Geolocation API.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure both properties are present with the correct TypeScript types (number) and have default numeric values (like 0).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class doesn't yet have the required latitude and longitude properties. Add two public properties with type number and default values inside the class body.

steps.title: Initialize error state property
steps.instruction: Add an errorMessage property of type string to the LocationComponent class to store potential error messages from geolocation operations.
steps.hint: Inside the LocationComponent class, declare a new property with type annotation: errorMessage: string;
steps.expectedOutcome: The component class now has an errorMessage property that can store string error messages.
successCriteria: The LocationComponent class contains a property named errorMessage with type string.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the errorMessage property to store potential geolocation errors.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've added a property named errorMessage with the correct type annotation (string).
steps.feedbackWrong: The errorMessage property is missing or incorrect. Please add a string property named errorMessage to the LocationComponent class.

steps.title: Define getCurrentLocation method
steps.instruction: Inside the LocationComponent class, add an async method named getCurrentLocation that calls Geolocation.getCurrentPosition() and stores the result in a temporary variable (we'll handle updating the state in the next step).
steps.hint: Use the async keyword before the method name. Inside the method, call await Geolocation.getCurrentPosition() and assign the result to a variable.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an async getCurrentLocation method that retrieves the current GPS position using Capacitor's Geolocation API.
successCriteria: The method should be async, named getCurrentLocation, and call Geolocation.getCurrentPosition() with await.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the async method that will fetch the GPS coordinates. The next step will handle processing the position data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the method is async and correctly calls Geolocation.getCurrentPosition(). Check that you're using await with the API call.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method doesn't match the requirements. It should be an async method named getCurrentLocation that calls Geolocation.getCurrentPosition().

steps.title: Handle location data in getCurrentLocation
steps.instruction: Inside the getCurrentLocation method, extract the coordinates from the Geolocation response and assign them to the latitude and longitude properties.
steps.hint: The Geolocation.getCurrentPosition() promise resolves with a Position object containing a coords property. Access latitude and longitude from coords.
steps.expectedOutcome: The getCurrentLocation method now extracts the latitude and longitude from the Geolocation response and stores them in the component's properties.
successCriteria: The getCurrentLocation method should assign values to this.latitude and this.longitude from the coordinates.coords object.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully extracted the coordinates from the Geolocation response and stored them in the component's properties.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're assigning both latitude and longitude from coordinates.coords.
steps.feedbackWrong: The getCurrentLocation method should extract latitude and longitude from the Geolocation response and assign them to this.latitude and this.longitude.

steps.title: Add error handling to getCurrentLocation
steps.instruction: Wrap the Geolocation.getCurrentPosition() call inside your getCurrentLocation method with a try-catch block. In the catch block, assign an error message string to the existing errorMessage property.
steps.hint: Use try { ... } catch (error) { ... } syntax. Inside catch, set this.errorMessage to a descriptive string like 'Failed to get location'.
steps.expectedOutcome: The getCurrentLocation method now includes error handling with try-catch, setting errorMessage when Geolocation fails.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added error handling to your location method. The try-catch block will now catch any errors from Geolocation.getCurrentPosition() and store them in errorMessage.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close! Make sure you've wrapped the Geolocation call in both try and catch blocks, and that you're setting this.errorMessage inside the catch block.
steps.feedbackWrong: The getCurrentLocation method should include a try-catch block around the Geolocation call, with errorMessage being set in the catch block.

steps.title: Update template to display location data
steps.instruction: Add Angular interpolation to the component's template to display the latitude and longitude properties from your component class.
steps.hint: Use double curly braces {{ }} to bind component properties in the template. For example: {{ latitude }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will show the latitude and longitude values when they are set by the getCurrentLocation method.
successCriteria: The template should contain interpolation expressions {{ latitude }} and {{ longitude }}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added interpolation to display the location coordinates in the template.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're using the correct property names (latitude and longitude) inside the double curly braces.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the required interpolation expressions. Remember to use {{ latitude }} and {{ longitude }} to display the coordinate values.

steps.title: Add error display to template
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add a paragraph element that uses *ngIf to display the errorMessage property when it has a value.
steps.hint: Use Angular's *ngIf directive to conditionally show the error message. The paragraph should only appear when errorMessage is truthy.
steps.analogousExample: {{ errorMessage }}
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now includes conditional error display that shows the error message when present.
successCriteria: The template should contain a paragraph element with *ngIf="errorMessage" that displays {{ errorMessage }}.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added conditional error display to your template. The error message will now appear only when there's an actual error.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but check that you've included both the *ngIf directive and the interpolation for errorMessage.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet show the error message conditionally. Make sure to add a paragraph with *ngIf that displays errorMessage when it exists.

steps.title: Add get location button
steps.instruction: Add a button element to your template that triggers the getCurrentLocation method when clicked.
steps.hint: Use Angular's event binding syntax (click)="getCurrentLocation()" on a button element.
steps.analogousExample:
<!-- Example of a button with click event binding -->
<button (click)="handleClick()">Click Me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: The template now contains a button that will call the getCurrentLocation method when clicked.
successCriteria: The button element must include (click)="getCurrentLocation()" event binding.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added a button that triggers location retrieval when clicked.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added a button, but it's missing the (click) event binding to call getCurrentLocation().
steps.feedbackWrong: The button element is not properly configured to trigger the getCurrentLocation method.

steps.title: Add loading state and improve UX
steps.instruction: Add a boolean property named 'isLoading' to your component class to track when the location is being fetched.
steps.hint: Declare a new property in the LocationComponent class with type boolean and an initial value.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a new property to track loading state, which will be used in the next steps to improve UX.
successCriteria: The component class contains a property named 'isLoading' of type boolean with an initial value.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the isLoading property. This will allow us to show a loading indicator while fetching location data.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you've declared 'isLoading' as a boolean property with an initial value in the LocationComponent class.
steps.feedbackWrong: The isLoading property wasn't added correctly. Please add a boolean property named 'isLoading' to the LocationComponent class.
